text:
alex: Quick sync — I ran a few long tails of the continuous-batching load and the profiler shows batch growth + padding is dominating GPU reserved memory once KV cache warms up. snapshots attached in the notebook link :eyes:

maria: Can you paste the critical stack traces / kernel names? curious if kernel switch is causing temp buffers to stick around.

alex: Sure — key things: `gemm_fp16_opt` spikes when seq len increases, and we see workspace blowup from `layernorm_fwd` path. also allocator live-set grows because reused buffers aren't recycled across batch shape changes.

cheng: OOM repro? or just high watermark?

alex: No hard OOM in prod yet, but local run hit `CUDA out of memory` when we force a big padding delta. High-watermark ~ 95% reserved. Reproducer steps in the gist: small loop with seq mix 32/128/512, enable kv-cache warming for second and third iter.

sam: That matches earlier theory — KV cache increases per-seq overhead and forces padding to grow nonlinearly. Two levers: (1) allocator tuning to allow faster free-to-reuse across kernels, (2) batch trimming heuristics to cap padding for tail-heavy mixes.

maria: Do we have telemetry showing frequency of those tall tails? if rare, a conservative fallback (force smaller kernel) might be ok.

alex: Telemetry: 7% of requests hit >256 seq, but they account for ~28% of token-time due to padding. So not rare for some customers.

cheng: On allocator: are we talking about freelist fragmentation or slab internal waste?

alex: Mostly slab internal waste + fragmentation when buffers are retained in different size classes; we saw cross-class leftover of ~120MB after warmup. Also the reclaim path is too slow during kernel switch so buffers sit idle.

sam: Idea: implement a short-lived buffer pool eviction for kernels that increase workspace requirement — evict small freelist entries that haven't been used in X ms. Tradeoff: possible small alloc latency.

maria: Could we get similar benefit by forcing kernel-choice stability (avoid switching to large workspace kernels unless batch shape stable)? Kernel selection policy tweak might be lower risk.

alex: I tried a quick patch to prefer lower-workspace kernel when batch variance > threshold. Reduced high-watermark by ~18% in the loop. PR draft: #4112. But throughput for steady long sequences dropped 6%.

cheng: Hmm. If we can do auto-fallback that detects sustained long-seq window and then switches up, we can get both. Need hysteresis.

infra-bot: deploy-check: preflight passed for branch alex/trim-kernel-policy; no perf regression in baseline microbench.

sam: Also need to account for KV cache shadowing — when kv-cache grows we should bias towards kernel with better KV locality to avoid duplicated buffers living in host+device.

maria: Agree. Also add targeted telemetry for per-seq buffer occupancy by size class (not just total reserved). that will help tune eviction thresholds.

alex: Action items: 1) cheng will prototype freelist eviction (short TTL) and measure latency impact. 2) I will iterate PR #4112 to add hysteresis and an opt-in feature flag. 3) sam to add size-class telemetry and a dashboard tile.

cheng: I can start today, will push a small bench and post numbers by EOD tomorrow.

sam: I'll make the dashboard and include a synthetic that mixes KV warmup shapes.

maria: Thanks — if we can shave ~15% high-watermark without hurting steady throughput we're in good shape. :thumbsup:

alex: Great. tagging this thread in the perf board. Will update with benchmarks and heap diffs.

infra-bot: incident-check: no open incidents related to OOMs on prod clusters in last 30d.

sam: One more note — consider buffer reuse hints at kernel dispatch time (provide a reuse token so kernels can compile with buffer aliasing in mind). low-risk prototype later.

alex: Noted. We'll revisit after the eviction + kernel-policy experiments.

maria: cheers, everyone.
